title: Why a straw looks bent in a glass of water
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature

Why does a swimming pool look shallower than it is?

explain.say: Put a straw in a glass of water and it seems to snap at the surface. The straw is fine; the light coming from it is what bends.

faq.a: Refraction is the bending of light when it passes at a slant from one material into another, like from water into air. It happens because light travels at different speeds in different materials.

faq.q: Why does light speed up in air?
faq.a: Light travels fastest in empty space. In water it is slowed by interacting with the water molecules, to about 225 thousand kilometres a second, so when it leaves water for air it speeds up again.
asks: How fast is light in water?

faq.q: Why does a swimming pool look shallower than it is?
faq.a: Light from the bottom bends as it leaves the water, so your brain thinks it came from a point higher up. A pool looks only about three quarters of its real depth, which can be dangerous.
asks: Why is the water deeper than it looks?

faq.q: Does the straw look bent if I look straight down?
faq.a: No. Light coming straight up, at right angles to the surface, does not change direction, so looking straight down the straw looks normal. Refraction only bends light that hits at a slant.
asks: Why does the bend change when I move my head?

faq.q: Why is it hard to grab a fish in a stream?
faq.a: Refraction makes the fish appear higher and closer than it really is. Herons and kingfishers learn to aim lower, below where the fish seems to be.
asks: Why do I miss things underwater?

facts: Light travels at about 225,000 kilometres per second in water, about three quarters of its speed in air.
Water has a refractive index of about 1.33, so pools look about three quarters as deep as they really are.

quiz.say: A pool sign says 2 metres deep, but the pool looks shallower. About how deep does it look?
quiz.why: Refraction makes water look about three quarters of its real depth, and three quarters of 2 metres is 1.5 metres.

wrong.1: Refraction makes water look shallower, not deeper.
wrong.2: Bent light makes the bottom appear raised.
